English: Prayer Stand
A simple wooden stand where prayer scrolls are read aloud. Serves as the first meeting point for a nomadic Jewish community.
Stone Marker
A sturdy stone pillar inscribed with blessings, marking the communitys gathering place for worship and ritual.
Wooden Pavilion
A roofed wooden structure providing shelter for prayer, study, and community decision-making.
Teaching Room
A dedicated space for communal teaching and the sharing of sacred knowledge.
Torah Chamber
A reinforced tent or wagon safeguarding Torah scrolls, symbolizing the growing permanence of the faith.
Sanctuary Hall
A large, semi-permanent canvas hall where the entire clan gathers for major festivals and prayers, fostering unity.
Ritual Pavilion
A richly decorated pavilion for life events, ceremonies, and hosting rabbis, strengthening the spiritual bonds of the clan.
Community Synagogue
A permanent, sturdy tent or wooden building serving as the heart of Jewish community life, with space for worship, study, and governance.
Scholars Hall
A center of learning and legal debate, attracting renowned scholars and teachers to the clan, invigorating Jewish tradition and unity.
Grand Synagogue
A grand, imposing structure of stone and wood, visible for miles, serving as the religious and cultural beacon of all nomadic Jews in the region.
